issue.title: Feature Request: Add Optional PDF Optimization During File Upload
issue.body:
**Feature Request: Add Optional PDF Optimization During File Upload**

Introduce an optional **"Optimize"** checkbox in the File Uploader that compresses PDF files before they are stored. This would help reduce storage usage, backup size, and upload/download times without affecting existing workflows.

**Problem:**
ERPNext users frequently upload PDF documents such as invoices, purchase orders, quotations, HR documents, manuals, and quality records. Many of these PDFs contain scanned images or unnecessary metadata, making them significantly larger than required.

Over time, this results in:
Increased file storage requirements

Currently, Frappe stores PDFs exactly as uploaded, with no option to optimize them.

**Proposed Solution**
Add an "Optimize PDF" checkbox to the File Uploader.
I have committed a proposed solution:
https://github.com/frappe/frappe/commit/f28020b25046fc2f23a01adac276515ebb324c21

**Workflow**:
User selects a PDF file.
An Optimize checkbox is displayed.
If enabled, the PDF is optimized before being saved.
If disabled, the original PDF is stored unchanged.

The optimization should preserve document readability while reducing file size.

**Benefits**
Reduce PDF size (often 30–55%, depending on the document)
e.g.:
Original Size : 12.4 MB
Optimized Size: 5.8 MB
Space Saved   : 53%

issue.title: Text Editor stores pasted images with absolute URL (node.src instead of getAttribute)
issue.body: ## Description of the issue The Quill image blot override in `frappe/public/js/frappe/form/controls/text_editor.js` reads the image source via the DOM property `node.src` in `MyImage.value(node)`. The property always resolves to an absolute URL, while `getAttribute("src")` returns the attribute as written. As a result, images inserted into a Text Editor field (paste, drag and drop, resize, or any Delta round trip) end up stored as `https:///private/files/?fid=` instead of the relative `/private/files/?fid=` that the upload returned. Relative file URLs are the convention everywhere else in Frappe (File.file_url, Attach fields, Image fields). Absolute URLs in stored HTML break when the site host changes, when a site is cloned or restored under another domain, and they are the reason images are missing in Chrome generated PDFs on version-16, where the request interceptor does not serve `/private/files/` (see #40394, #40425, #40510). The same code is present on develop, version-16 and version-15. ## Context information Output of `bench version` frappe 16.31.0 erpnext 16.33.0 Also reproduced on develop by reading the source (MyImage.value, `src: node.src`). ## Steps to reproduce the issue 1. Open any document with a Text Editor field, for example Quotation, Introduction Text. 2. Paste an image from the clipboard. The upload succeeds and the editor shows the image. 3. Save and inspect the stored HTML (for example via the API or the database). ### Observed result `` ### Expected result `` ## Additional information Suggested fix, one line in `MyImage.value`: ```diff static value(node) { return { align: node.align, style: node.style.cssText, - src: node.src, + src: node.getAttribute("src"), }; } ``` Verified in the browser on 16.31.0 with this change applied via a client script: paste and Delta round trip keep the relative path, while the original code turns it into the absolute URL. I am happy to open a PR for develop with backports to version-16-hotfix and version-15-hotfix if a maintainer prefers that route.

issue.title: Legacy parallel implementation of `get_max_file_size`
issue.body:
This is a minor cleanup issue.

A legacy `get_max_file_size` exists here:

https://github.com/frappe/frappe/blob/b0ae2b1421797241cdbf802a0cb4f770b7e7ce66/frappe/utils/file_manager.py#L210-L211

while a newer, more robust implementation exists here:

https://github.com/frappe/frappe/blob/b0ae2b1421797241cdbf802a0cb4f770b7e7ce66/frappe/core/api/file.py#L81-L87

Ideally the former should just delegate to the latter; or be completely replaced by the latter.

issue.title: Currency label duplicated instead of replaced: "Rate (Company Currency) (SAR)" — regression from #40187
issue.body: ## Description of the issue `frm.set_currency_labels()` appends the currency to a field's label without removing any parenthetical already present in that label, so labels that end in a placeholder suffix are rendered twice over. On any ERPNext transaction this shows up as: - `Taxes and Charges Added (Company Currency) (SAR)` - `Claimed Landed Cost Amount (Company Currency) (SAR)` - `Rate (Company Currency) (SAR)` — in the **items** child table This is a regression introduced by #40187 (merged 2026-06-22), backported to `version-15-hotfix` (#40190) and `version-16-hotfix` (#40191). Before that change the method stripped parentheticals before appending: ```js var label = __(docfield.label || "", null, docfield.parent).replace(/\([^\)]*\)/g, ""); ``` so `Rate (Company Currency)` became `Rate` and then `Rate (SAR)`. #40187 replaced that with a pristine-label capture and no stripping at all: ```js if (docfield._original_label === undefined) { docfield._original_label = docfield.label; } var label = __(docfield._original_label || "", null, docfield.parent); ``` The intent of #40187 is sound — the blanket regex also destroyed legitimate parentheticals such as `Rate (ex-tax)` — but removing the stripping entirely over-corrects, and nothing now handles the placeholder case the old regex was covering. Both the document scope and the grid scope are affected, since `set_currency_labels()` builds `field_label_map` and `grid_field_label_map` with the same concatenation. In ERPNext this affects **160 fields across 38 doctypes**, 23 of them child tables — every Currency field whose `options` is `Company:company:default_currency` and whose label ends in `(Company Currency)`. ## Context information (for bug reports) **Output of `bench version`** ``` erpnext 16.35.0 version-16 (12cd563) frappe 16.34.0 version-16 (c1f1e8e) ``` Also reproducible on `version-16-hotfix` and `develop` — the affected code is identical on all branches that received #40187 or its backports. ## Steps to reproduce the issue 1. On a company whose default currency is e.g. `SAR`, open a new **Purchase Invoice**. 2. Select a supplier and add one item. 3. Expand the **Currency and Price List** section and set a supplier currency different from the company currency, so the company-currency fields become visible. 4. Look at the parent field **Taxes and Charges Added**, and at the **Rate (Company Currency)** column inside the items grid. ### Observed result Labels carry both the placeholder and the resolved currency: ``` Taxes and Charges Added (Company Currency) (SAR) Rate (Company Currency) (SAR) ``` ### Expected result The placeholder is replaced by the resolved currency, as it was before #40187: ``` Taxes and Charges Added (SAR) Rate (SAR) ``` ### Stacktrace / full error message None — this is a rendering issue, no exception is raised. ## Related #42651 (*fix: refresh child currency fields and prevent grid symbol overlap*, open against `develop`) touches child-table currency rendering, but addresses stale currency after a parent change and symbol/amount overlap for wide symbols. It does not cover the duplicated label, so this looks adjacent rather than a duplicate. ## Possible direction Rather than restoring the blanket `\([^\)]*\)` regex (which is what #40187 correctly removed), `set_currency_labels()` could strip only a trailing parenthetical that is a currency placeholder before appending, leaving labels like `Rate (ex-tax)` untouched. That would keep the guarantee #40187 added while restoring the behaviour ERPNext's labels rely on.

issue.title: FileUploader: "Upload file" button misaligned when used with a custom wrapper
Administrator's placeholder email is globally unsubscribed, so no transactional auth mail (2FA enrolment, OTP reset) can ever reach it
issue.body:
## Description of the issue

The built-in `Administrator` user is installed with a placeholder address that is then globally unsubscribed, so **no mail can ever reach `Administrator`** — including transactional auth mail such as 2FA enrolment and OTP secret reset.

`frappe/utils/install.py`:

```python
{
	"doctype": "User",
	"name": "Administrator",
	"first_name": "Administrator",
	"email": "admin@example.com",
	...
}
```

`frappe/desk/page/setup_wizard/install_fixtures.py`:

```python
def add_unsubscribe():
	for unsubscribe in [
		{"email": "admin@example.com", "global_unsubscribe": 1},
		{"email": "guest@example.com", "global_unsubscribe": 1},
	]:
```

Nothing in the setup wizard ever replaces the Administrator address, so on the overwhelming majority of sites it stays `admin@example.com` for the life of the site.

The unsubscribe entry is enforced in `QueueBuilder`, **before** the queue row is written:

```python
# frappe/email/doctype/email_queue/email_queue.py
def process(self, send_now=False) -> EmailQueue | None:
	final_recipients = self.final_recipients()
	...
	if not (final_recipients + self.final_cc() + self.final_bcc()):
		return []
```

So the mail is not "queued and held" — it does not exist. There is no **Email Queue** record for a System Manager to inspect, no failure row, and no error. `frappe.sendmail()` returns `[]`, and `send_token_via_email()` turns that into `False`:

```python
# frappe/twofactor.py
return bool(
	frappe.sendmail(
		recipients=user_email,
		...
	)
)
```

A third place repeats the same assumption — `get_user_info()` filters the two placeholder addresses out of every role-based recipient list:

```python
# frappe/core/doctype/role/role.py
if enabled and user_info not in ["admin@example.com", "guest@example.com"]:
	info_list.append(user_info)
```

This was harmless while `Administrator` was exempt from 2FA. Since #41687 removed that exemption (shipped in v15.118.0 / v16.31.0), it is now the reason `Administrator` cannot enrol in 2FA at all — see #42852.

## Context information (for bug reports)

**Output of `bench version`**

```
frappe >= 15.118.0
frappe >= 16.31.0
frappe develop (v17)
```

The placeholder address and the unsubscribe fixture predate this and exist on every version; only the consequence is new.

## Steps to reproduce the issue

1. Fresh site, working outgoing **Email Account**, **System Settings → Enable Two Factor Authentication** checked, `Two Factor Method = OTP App` (the default).
2. Log in as `Administrator`.
3. Check **Email Queue** as a System Manager.

### Observed result

* Login page: *"Verification code email not sent. Please contact Administrator."*
* **Email Queue**: no record at all — not `Not Sent`, not `Error`, nothing.
* Same for `reset_otp_secret("Administrator")`: the notification mail is dropped the same way.

### Expected result

Transactional auth mail addressed to `Administrator` should be deliverable, and a delivery failure should be visible in **Email Queue** rather than silently discarded.

### Proposed fix (path 2 of 2)

PR: #42855

1. Install `Administrator` with `admin@frappe.local` instead of `admin@example.com`, so the account has an address that is not on the global unsubscribe list and that an operator can point a catch-all at.
2. Stop inserting the global unsubscribe row for the Administrator address in `install_fixtures.add_unsubscribe()` (`guest@example.com` stays unsubscribed — Guest should never receive mail).
3. Drop the Administrator address from the `get_user_info()` skip-list in `role.py` for the same reason.
4. Ship a patch for existing sites that rewrites the Administrator address **only if it is still the untouched placeholder**, and removes the stale `Email Unsubscribe` row.

With that in place, `Administrator` can complete OTP App enrolment: the QR mail is queued, a System Manager (or a catch-all mailbox) can read it from **Email Queue**, and TOTP can be registered.

### Known limitation of this path

A site with **no outgoing Email Account configured** still cannot deliver the enrolment mail, and `Administrator` is still stuck at the 2FA prompt — with the difference that the failure is now visible in **Email Queue** instead of invisible. If 2FA is to stay mandatory for `Administrator`, that case wants a follow-up (for example, refusing to enable 2FA without a working outgoing account, or a `bench` escape hatch).

That is why the smaller alternative — reverting #41687 so `Administrator` is exempt again — is tracked separately in #42852 with PR #42854. The two paths are mutually exclusive; **please pick one**.

type="button"

on buttons generated by the Frappe Button control.

I have tested this change locally and confirmed that it prevents the unintended button activation.

issue.title: log_error stores frame locals (with_context=True) by default, so a failed HTTP call writes the live credential into Error Log
issue.body:
## Description of the issue

`frappe.log_error()` stores the traceback **with frame locals** by default (`frappe/utils/error.py`, `frappe.get_traceback(with_context=True)`), and the background job runner calls it that way for every failed job (`frappe/utils/background_jobs.py`, `execute_job`: `frappe.log_error(title=method_name)`), as does `Scheduled Job Type.update_scheduler_log` for a failed scheduled job (`details = frappe.get_traceback(with_context=True)`).

`get_traceback(with_context=True)` prints every local variable of every frame, library frames included, up to 1000 characters each. The sanitizer only hides a variable whose *name* matches `password|passwd|secret|token|key|pwd`, and masks dict values only for keys spelled exactly that way. A failed HTTP call in a job therefore writes the live credential into `Error Log`:

- a local named `headers = {"Authorization": "Token abc:SECRET"}` is stored in full (the name `headers` does not match, and the dict key `Authorization` does not match);
- a `frappe._dict` holding `stripe_secret_key` is stored in full;
- `stripe.Customer.retrieve(...)` against an unreachable host produces a ~11 KB traceback that includes `'Authorization': 'Bearer sk_test_…'` from the stripe library's own request frame.

`Error Log` is readable by System Manager, is shipped to Sentry when telemetry is on (`frappe/utils/error.py` forwards `f"{title}\n{traceback}"`), and is commonly exported or pulled by monitoring. A plain `get_traceback()` carries the frames a developer needs to locate the failure without the locals.

## Steps to reproduce

1. On any site, enqueue a job that makes an authenticated HTTP call to an unreachable host:

```python
def job():
    import requests
    headers = {"Authorization": "Token abc:SECRET"}
    requests.get("https://127.0.0.1:9", headers=headers, timeout=1)

frappe.enqueue("myapp.job", queue="short")
```

2. Open the resulting `Error Log` row. Its `error` field contains `'Authorization': 'Token abc:SECRET'` from the `requests` frames (and `headers = {...}` from `job`'s own frame).

Observed on version-16 (16.25.0) and the same lines are on `develop`.

## Suggested fix

Store the plain traceback by default; keep the with-context form opt-in for developers who want it on a dev site.

```diff
--- a/frappe/utils/error.py
+++ b/frappe/utils/error.py
@@ def log_error(title=None, message=None, reference_doctype=None, reference_name=None, *, defer_insert=False):
-	traceback = frappe.as_unicode(traceback or frappe.get_traceback(with_context=True))
+	traceback = frappe.as_unicode(
+		traceback or frappe.get_traceback(with_context=bool(frappe.conf.developer_mode))
+	)
```

and the same change in `frappe/core/doctype/scheduled_job_type/scheduled_job_type.py` (`update_scheduler_log`, the `details` field on a failed job).

Related: #42523 (the forked worker exits before the Sentry transport flushes), found in the same investigation.

issue.title: Success Action alert message not translated (baked into DB at install time, not passed through __() on display)
issue.body:
## Description

The "Success Action" alert shown after submitting a document (e.g. "Purchase Invoice has been submitted successfully") is never translated for the active user language, even when a matching translation exists in the translation files.

## Root cause

1. `erpnext/setup/default_success_action.py` builds the message using a translatable template:
   ```python
   def get_message(doctype):
       return _("{0} has been submitted successfully").format(doctype)
   ```
2. `create_default_success_action()` in `erpnext/setup/install.py` calls this **once**, during `after_install`, and stores the resulting string permanently in the `message` / `first_success_message` fields of a `Success Action` document (one per doctype: Purchase Receipt, Purchase Invoice, Quotation, Sales Order, Delivery Note, Sales Invoice).
3. At display time, `frappe/public/js/frappe/form/success_action.js` reads this stored value directly and shows it as-is:
   ```js
   let message = count === 1 ? setting.first_success_message : setting.message;
   ...
   frappe.show_alert({ message: message, body: html, indicator: "green" }, ...);
   ```
   Notice `message` is **not** passed through `__()` here, unlike the button labels a few lines below (`__(action.label)`).

Because the string is baked into the database at install/migrate time (in whatever language was active then, typically English) and never re-translated in JS, adding a translation to `pl.csv` (or any other language file) for `"{0} has been submitted successfully"` or for the literal per-doctype strings (e.g. `"Purchase Invoice has been submitted successfully"`) has **no effect** on what the user sees — the alert is permanently stuck in the install-time language.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Install/create a site where the site language is English at install time (default).
2. Switch the site language to any other language (e.g. Polish) afterwards.
3. Submit a Purchase Invoice (or any of the other affected doctypes).
4. Observe the green success alert — it still shows the English text "Purchase Invoice has been submitted successfully" instead of the translated string, even though a translation exists.

Confirmed directly in the database:
```python
frappe.get_all("Success Action", filters={"ref_doctype": "Purchase Invoice"},
    fields=["name", "message", "first_success_message"])
# [{'name': 'Purchase Invoice', 'message': 'Purchase Invoice has been submitted successfully', ...}]
```
while `System Settings.language` is `pl`.

## Expected Behavior

The success alert message should be translated according to the current user/site language at display time, similar to how the action button labels (`New`, `Print`, `Email`) are translated via `__()`.

## Possible Fix

- Store only the doctype name (or a translation key) in the `Success Action` document, and build/translate the final message string in JS via `__("{0} has been submitted successfully", [__(setting.ref_doctype)])` at display time in `success_action.js`, instead of baking the formatted, language-locked string into the database once at install time.

## Versions

- Frappe/ERPNext: develop branch (v16)

issue.title: Currency label duplicated instead of replaced: "Rate (Company Currency) (SAR)" — regression from #40187
issue.body: ## Description of the issue `frm.set_currency_labels()` appends the currency to a field's label without removing any parenthetical already present in that label, so labels that end in a placeholder suffix are rendered twice over. On any ERPNext transaction this shows up as: - `Taxes and Charges Added (Company Currency) (SAR)` - `Claimed Landed Cost Amount (Company Currency) (SAR)` - `Rate (Company Currency) (SAR)` — in the **items** child table This is a regression introduced by #40187 (merged 2026-06-22), backported to `version-15-hotfix` (#40190) and `version-16-hotfix` (#40191). Before that change the method stripped parentheticals before appending: ```js var label = __(docfield.label || "", null, docfield.parent).replace(/\([^\)]*\)/g, ""); ``` so `Rate (Company Currency)` became `Rate` and then `Rate (SAR)`. #40187 replaced that with a pristine-label capture and no stripping at all: ```js if (docfield._original_label === undefined) { docfield._original_label = docfield.label; } var label = __(docfield._original_label || "", null, docfield.parent); ``` The intent of #40187 is sound — the blanket regex also destroyed legitimate parentheticals such as `Rate (ex-tax)` — but removing the stripping entirely over-corrects, and nothing now handles the placeholder case the old regex was covering. Both the document scope and the grid scope are affected, since `set_currency_labels()` builds `field_label_map` and `grid_field_label_map` with the same concatenation. In ERPNext this affects **160 fields across 38 doctypes**, 23 of them child tables — every Currency field whose `options` is `Company:company:default_currency` and whose label ends in `(Company Currency)`. ## Context information (for bug reports) **Output of `bench version`** ``` erpnext 16.35.0 version-16 (12cd563) frappe 16.34.0 version-16 (c1f1e8e) ``` Also reproducible on `version-16-hotfix` and `develop` — the affected code is identical on all branches that received #40187 or its backports. ## Steps to reproduce the issue 1. On a company whose default currency is e.g. `SAR`, open a new **Purchase Invoice**. 2. Select a supplier and add one item. 3. Expand the **Currency and Price List** section and set a supplier currency different from the company currency, so the company-currency fields become visible. 4. Look at the parent field **Taxes and Charges Added**, and at the **Rate (Company Currency)** column inside the items grid. ### Observed result Labels carry both the placeholder and the resolved currency: ``` Taxes and Charges Added (Company Currency) (SAR) Rate (Company Currency) (SAR) ``` ### Expected result The placeholder is replaced by the resolved currency, as it was before #40187: ``` Taxes and Charges Added (SAR) Rate (SAR) ``` ### Stacktrace / full error message None — this is a rendering issue, no exception is raised. ## Related #42651 (*fix: refresh child currency fields and prevent grid symbol overlap*, open against `develop`) touches child-table currency rendering, but addresses stale currency after a parent change and symbol/amount overlap for wide symbols. It does not cover the duplicated label, so this looks adjacent rather than a duplicate. ## Possible direction Rather than restoring the blanket `\([^\)]*\)` regex (which is what #40187 correctly removed), `set_currency_labels()` could strip only a trailing parenthetical that is a currency placeholder before appending, leaving labels like `Rate (ex-tax)` untouched. That would keep the guarantee #40187 added while restoring the behaviour ERPNext's labels rely on.

issue.title: install_app() commits Patch Log stamps before after_install runs, leaving a failed install unrepairable by bench migrate
issue.body:
## Description

`install_app()` commits the Patch Log stamps for an app **before** running that app's `after_install` hook. If `after_install` then fails, its work is rolled back but the patch stamps survive, because they were already committed.

The site is left in a state that `bench migrate` can never repair: every patch that would recreate the missing schema is already recorded as executed, so migrate skips it — permanently.

## Cause

`frappe/installer.py`, lines 357-361:

```python
	if set_as_patched:
		set_all_patches_as_completed(name)   # L358

	for after_install in app_hooks.after_install or []:
		frappe.get_attr(after_install)()     # L361
```

`set_all_patches_as_completed()` (L567) commits immediately:

```python
def set_all_patches_as_completed(app):
	patches = get_patches_from_app(app)
	for patch in patches:
		frappe.get_doc({"doctype": "Patch Log", "patch": patch}).insert(ignore_permissions=True)
	frappe.db.commit()
```

Pre-stamping is correct in itself — a fresh install already has the final schema, so the patches are genuinely redundant. The assumption only holds if `after_install` actually completes, and nothing enforces that. ERPNext's `after_install` is a 20-call sequence with a single `frappe.db.commit()` at the very end (`erpnext/setup/install.py`), so an exception anywhere discards all of it while the stamps remain.

## Observed on a production site

Fresh Ubuntu 24.04 box, ERPNext installed 2026-08-15. Symptom was `Unknown column 'tabContact.is_billing_contact'`.

All 57 `erpnext.patches.v16_0` patches carry install-time timestamps spanning **142 milliseconds** — they were stamped, not executed:

```sql
select count(*), min(creation), max(creation)
  from `tabPatch Log` where patch like 'erpnext.patches.v16_0%';
-- 57 | 2026-08-15 23:57:32.516469 | 2026-08-15 23:57:32.658327
```

Everything `after_install` should have created is absent:

| Created by `after_install` | Present |
|---|---|
| `Contact.is_billing_contact` | no |
| `Address.tax_category` | no |
| `Address.is_your_company_address` | no |
| Custom Field rows for Address/Contact | 0 |
| Incoterms (`create_incoterms`) | 0 |
| Default Operations (`make_default_operations`) | 0 |
| Letter Head (`create_letter_head`) | 0 |

The custom fields written *before* that point in the install (Quotation, Customer at 23:57:27) are present, so the install itself progressed normally up to the hook.

**`bench migrate` does not fix it.** I ran it three times on this site, including across an upgrade from erpnext 16.32.1 to 16.32.3. `is_billing_contact` remained absent every time — as expected, since the patch is stamped.

A second site of ours that was upgraded v15 → v16 in place has all three fields, because there the patch was genuinely pending and ran. Its 57 `v16_0` stamps span 68 days rather than 142 ms. The bug only reaches sites installed fresh.

## Why this keeps coming back

Same root cause, reported three times and closed each time with a workaround rather than a fix:

- frappe/erpnext#43509 (Oct 2024) — closed after "upgrading resolved the issue"
- frappe/erpnext#53344 (Mar 2026) — closed, last comment `is_billing_contact is not exist in Doctype Contact`
- frappe/erpnext#57766 (Aug 2026) — closed; the reporter found the exact mechanism: *"patch log is created but the custom fields does not create"*, fixed by running the patch by hand

The manual remedy works, but nothing prevents the next fresh install from landing in the same state.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Install an app whose `after_install` raises partway through (ERPNext reproduces this when any step in its 20-call sequence fails).
2. Observe the app is marked installed and all its patches are in `tabPatch Log`.
3. Run `bench migrate` — every patch is skipped, and the schema `after_install` should have created is still missing, with no way to recover through normal commands.

## Suggested fix

Order the two operations so the stamps can't outlive a failed hook. Either:

- run `after_install` **before** `set_all_patches_as_completed()`, so a raised exception aborts the install with no stamps written; or
- keep the order but roll the stamps back if `after_install` raises.

Either way a failed install stays recoverable by re-running it. It would also help if a failing `after_install` surfaced loudly instead of leaving a site that looks installed.

## Versions

```
frappe   16.31.0  version-16 (6a329d0)
erpnext  16.32.3  version-16 (11e0ba0)
hrms     16.16.0  version-16 (f281e8b)
```
MariaDB 10.11.14, Python 3.14.6, installed via bench (production setup).

This report asks for a backport of that behaviour, or the minimal patch below, to `version-16`.

**Affected code**

- `frappe/public/js/frappe/ui/sidebar/sidebar.js`: `set_workspace_sidebar()` (L665–L690), `resolve_sidebar()` (L709–L745), `filter_sidebars_from_app()` (L746–L756)
- `frappe/public/js/frappe/router.js`: `set_doctype_route()` L206 (`this.meta = meta`)

**Steps to reproduce**

1. Install any app besides erpnext that ships a Script Report and a Workspace Sidebar (or just a Module Def — Frappe auto-generates a sidebar per module via `auto_generate_sidebar_from_module()`). The report's `module` is the app's own module. Call the app `myapp`, the module `My Module`, the report `My Report`.
2. Open any ERPNext page that belongs to a different app, e.g. `/app/stock-entry` (module Stock, app erpnext). The Stock sidebar is shown.
3. Navigate in-app to the report — via the awesomebar (`Ctrl+K` → "My Report"), or by pasting `/app/query-report/My Report` in the URL bar.

**Expected**

The sidebar switches to `My Module` (the only sidebar that links to `My Report`), and the breadcrumb reads `My Module / My Report`.

**Actual**

The Stock sidebar stays. The breadcrumb reads `Stock / My Report`, because `set_workspace_breadcrumb()` in `breadcrumbs.js` derives the first crumb from `frappe.app.sidebar.sidebar_title`.

ERPNext's own reports are not affected: any stale module still belongs to app `erpnext`, so the app filter keeps their sidebars.

**Cause**

`set_workspace_sidebar(router)` passes `router?.meta?.module` into `resolve_sidebar()` as the "active module". But `router.meta` is only assigned in `set_doctype_route()` (router.js L206) — i.e. for DocType routes. For `query-report/*` (and `Workspaces/*`, pages, dashboards) it is never updated, so it still holds the meta of the *previous* DocType page.

`resolve_sidebar()` then does:

```js
// 3. narrow candidates to the active app
if (module) {
    candidates = this.filter_sidebars_from_app(
        candidates,
        frappe.boot.module_app[module.toLowerCase().replace(/[ -]/g, "_")]
    );
}
```

With `module = "Stock"` the app becomes `erpnext`; `filter_sidebars_from_app()` keeps only sidebars whose `app === "erpnext"`, which removes the third-party sidebar — the *only* candidate that actually links to the entity. `candidates` is now empty, rule 4 falls through to `resolve_module_sidebar("Stock")`, which returns the Stock sidebar, and the final `if (!sidebar_name && candidates.length > 0)` fallback never fires because the original candidates were discarded.

Two bugs compound:

1. The module used for narrowing is stale for non-DocType routes.
2. The app filter can throw away every candidate; when it does, the resolver prefers "a sidebar from the (wrong) app" over "the sidebar that links to the entity".

**Suggested fix**

Backporting develop's resolver is the complete fix. If that is too large for `version-16`, either of these alone fixes the reported case; both together are more robust.

a. In `resolve_sidebar()`, never let the app filter empty the list — fall back to the unfiltered candidates:

```js
if (module) {
    const app = frappe.boot.module_app[module.toLowerCase().replace(/[ -]/g, "_")];
    const same_app = this.filter_sidebars_from_app(candidates, app);
    if (same_app.length) candidates = same_app;
}
```

b. Use the entity's own module for reports instead of the stale `router.meta`. `frappe.boot.workspace_sidebar_item[*].items[*].report` already carries `ref_doctype` for report links, and `frappe.boot.all_reports[name].module` is available, so `set_workspace_sidebar()` could derive `module` for `query-report` routes from the report, and `set_doctype_route()` is not the only place `router.meta` should be refreshed (clearing `this.meta` on non-DocType routes would also stop the stale value from leaking).

A regression test (cypress spec) that navigates `stock-entry → query-report/<third-party report>` and asserts `frappe.app.sidebar.sidebar_title` would cover this on both branches.

**Workaround for app authors**

Ship a `Workspace Sidebar` + `Desktop Icon` for the module and, in an `app_include_js`, call `frappe.app.sidebar.setup("<Sidebar>")` on `frappe.router.on("change")` when the route points at one of the app's DocTypes or reports. Once the correct sidebar is active, rule 1 of the resolver ("current sidebar already links to this entity → keep it") holds on its own.

issue.title: log_error stores frame locals (with_context=True) by default, so a failed HTTP call writes the live credential into Error Log
issue.body:
## Description of the issue

`frappe.log_error()` stores the traceback **with frame locals** by default (`frappe/utils/error.py`, `frappe.get_traceback(with_context=True)`), and the background job runner calls it that way for every failed job (`frappe/utils/background_jobs.py`, `execute_job`: `frappe.log_error(title=method_name)`), as does `Scheduled Job Type.update_scheduler_log` for a failed scheduled job (`details = frappe.get_traceback(with_context=True)`).

`get_traceback(with_context=True)` prints every local variable of every frame, library frames included, up to 1000 characters each. The sanitizer only hides a variable whose *name* matches `password|passwd|secret|token|key|pwd`, and masks dict values only for keys spelled exactly that way. A failed HTTP call in a job therefore writes the live credential into `Error Log`:

- a local named `headers = {"Authorization": "Token abc:SECRET"}` is stored in full (the name `headers` does not match, and the dict key `Authorization` does not match);
- a `frappe._dict` holding `stripe_secret_key` is stored in full;
- `stripe.Customer.retrieve(...)` against an unreachable host produces a ~11 KB traceback that includes `'Authorization': 'Bearer sk_test_…'` from the stripe library's own request frame.

`Error Log` is readable by System Manager, is shipped to Sentry when telemetry is on (`frappe/utils/error.py` forwards `f"{title}\n{traceback}"`), and is commonly exported or pulled by monitoring. A plain `get_traceback()` carries the frames a developer needs to locate the failure without the locals.

## Steps to reproduce

1. On any site, enqueue a job that makes an authenticated HTTP call to an unreachable host:

```python
def job():
    import requests
    headers = {"Authorization": "Token abc:SECRET"}
    requests.get("https://127.0.0.1:9", headers=headers, timeout=1)

frappe.enqueue("myapp.job", queue="short")
```

2. Open the resulting `Error Log` row. Its `error` field contains `'Authorization': 'Token abc:SECRET'` from the `requests` frames (and `headers = {...}` from `job`'s own frame).

Observed on version-16 (16.25.0) and the same lines are on `develop`.

## Suggested fix

Store the plain traceback by default; keep the with-context form opt-in for developers who want it on a dev site.

```diff
--- a/frappe/utils/error.py
+++ b/frappe/utils/error.py
@@ def log_error(title=None, message=None, reference_doctype=None, reference_name=None, *, defer_insert=False):
-	traceback = frappe.as_unicode(traceback or frappe.get_traceback(with_context=True))
+	traceback = frappe.as_unicode(
+		traceback or frappe.get_traceback(with_context=bool(frappe.conf.developer_mode))
+	)
```

and the same change in `frappe/core/doctype/scheduled_job_type/scheduled_job_type.py` (`update_scheduler_log`, the `details` field on a failed job).

Related: #42523 (the forked worker exits before the Sentry transport flushes), found in the same investigation.

issue.title: User.user_type filter exemption missing on read-permission path — breaks Assign/Share for non-System Managers (regression in v16.33.0)
issue.body:
## Description of the issue

`User.user_type` (permlevel 1) is exempted from the filter-field permission check **only** on the `select`-permission path. Users who have **`read` (or `read` + `select`)** on `User` fall through to `get_permitted_fields()`, which has no such exemption, so `user_query` raises:

```
frappe.exceptions.PermissionError: You do not have permission to access field: User.user_type
```

`search_widget` swallows `PermissionError` and responds `404 "Method not found"`, so the user sees a red **"Not found — The resource you are looking for is not available"** dialog with no way to diagnose it.

This breaks, for every non-System-Manager who has `read` on User:

- **Assign** dialog (`assign_to.js` filters `{user_type: "System User", enabled: 1}`)
- **Share** dialog (`share.js`, same filter)
- HRMS approver link fields (`hrms/public/js/erpnext/department.js`)

Granting a *stronger* permission (`read`) removes an ability that `select` alone has — a privilege inversion. In the Role Permissions Manager, Read and Select are independent checkboxes, so the combination is a normal, expected configuration.

## Context information

```
frappe   16.34.0  version-16
erpnext  16.x     version-16
```

Introduced in **v16.33.0** (published 2026-09-01) by #40248.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Role Permissions Manager → Document Type `User` → role `Desk User`, Level 0 → tick **Read** (keep **Select** ticked).
2. Log in as a user who is not a System Manager.
3. Open any document → sidebar → **Assign** → **+**.
4. Dialog opens, then "Not found" appears and the *Assign To* list is empty. Network tab: `GET /api/method/frappe.desk.search.search_link?doctype=User&filters={"user_type":"System User","enabled":1}` → `404`.

Untick **Read** (stock config, select-only) and it works again.

## Root cause

#40248 removed `User` from the blanket `CORE_DOCTYPES` exemption in **both** permission paths:

- `frappe/model/__init__.py` → `get_permitted_fields()`: `if doctype in CORE_DOCTYPES and doctype != "User":`
- `frappe/database/query.py` → `_get_filterable_fields()`: `if doctype in PERMITTED_CORE_DOCTYPES and doctype != "User":`

but added the compensating `user_type` carve-out to only one of them:

```python
# frappe/database/query.py, select branch only
if doctype == "User":
    # user_type is permlevel 1 but not itself sensitive, and the built-in
    # Link-field search (user.user_query) filters by it for every select-only caller
    permlevel_0_fields.add("user_type")
```

`Engine.get_permission_type()` returns `"select"` only when `frappe.only_has_select_perm()` is true, i.e. select **and not** read. With read set, the query takes the `else` branch → `_get_cached_permitted_fields()` → `get_permitted_fields()` → no carve-out → `PermissionError`.

Note the file carries the comment *"any change here should also be made in `_get_filterable_fields` in query.py"*; the two paths are still out of sync in the other direction.

Why CI did not catch it: the regression test added in #37932, `test_core_doctype_filterable_fields_with_select_permission`, explicitly clears read before asserting:

```python
add_permission("User", test_role, 0, ptype="select")
update_permission_property("User", test_role, 0, "read", 0, validate=False)
```

so only the select-only combination is covered.

## Suggested fix

Either:

1. apply the same `user_type` exemption in `get_permitted_fields()` for `User`, or
2. preferably, skip filter-field permission checks for filters injected by trusted server-side standard queries — `user.user_query` sets `user_type` itself, it is never user input.

Plus a test covering the `read` + `select` combination.

Secondary: `search_widget` converting `PermissionError` into a `404 "Method not found"` web page makes this class of bug very hard to diagnose — the user-facing message is unrelated to the actual cause, and nothing is written to the Error Log.

## Related

- #37850 — Assign dialog throws permission error
- #37923 — Permission Error on MultiSelectPills
- #37932 — earlier fix, select path only
- #40248 — the change that introduced this

issue.body:
get_field_precision() (frappe/model/meta.py and the client-side frappe/public/js/frappe/model/meta.js) and fmt_money() (frappe/utils/data.py) all resolve the System Settings Currency Precision value the same way:

    precision = cint(frappe.db.get_default("currency_precision"))
    if not precision:
        ...fall back to the Number Format's own precision...

cint("0") is the integer 0, which is falsy in both Python and JavaScript, so an explicitly configured Currency Precision of 0 is indistinguishable from "not set" and silently discarded in favour of the Number Format's precision (typically 2 decimals).

Fixed by checking whether the stored default is actually unset (None or an empty string) instead of relying on truthiness, so 0 is treated as a valid, explicit value everywhere it's resolved.

Fixes #42058

issue.title: fix(model): allow list values for JSON fieldtypes in get_valid_dict
issue.body:
### Problem
Closes #42462.

When serializing a document via `as_dict()` / `get_valid_dict()`, `base_document.py` checked:
```python
if isinstance(value, list) and fieldtype not in table_fields:
    frappe.throw(_("Value for {0} cannot be a list").format(_(df.label, context=df.parent)))
```
This mistakenly threw a `ValidationError` when a valid `JSON` field type contained a Python `list` (e.g., `link_filters` in `DocField` containing `[{"key": "val"}]`), breaking serialization and operations like `remove_orphan_doctypes()` / `add_to_deleted_document()`. Furthermore, the JSON serialization branch only handled `isinstance(value, dict)` and missed lists.

### Solution
1. Excluded `fieldtype != "JSON"` from the list rejection guard in `get_valid_dict()`.
2. Updated the `JSON` dump serialization branch to handle `isinstance(value, (dict, list))`.
3. Added a unit test in `frappe/tests/test_base_document.py` (`test_get_valid_dict_json_field_with_list`) verifying that JSON list values are properly serialized to JSON strings without error, while non-JSON non-table fields continue to reject list values.

issue.title: Query Report Excel export writes Date/Datetime columns as text, breaking sort order
issue.body:
`frappe.desk.query_report.export_query` (used by every Script/Query Report's "Export" button, e.g. ERPNext's General Ledger) converts `Date`/`Datetime` columns to display-formatted strings via `format_fields()` *before* handing the data to the Excel writer. `frappe.utils.xlsxutils.make_xlsx` only writes a native, sortable Excel date cell when it receives an actual `datetime.date`/`datetime.datetime` — a string is written as plain text, so Excel sorts the column alphabetically instead of chronologically (e.g. with System Settings Date Format `dd-mm-yyyy`: `01-07-2026, 01-08-2026, 02-07-2026, 02-08-2026` instead of date order).

CSV export is unaffected in practice (CSV has no cell types, so Excel re-parses the text as a date when it opens the file), and List View / Report View export (`frappe.desk.reportview.export_query`) is also unaffected — it doesn't stringify dates. The bug is specific to the Query Report export path.

**To Reproduce**

1. Open any Query/Script Report with a Date column (e.g. Accounting > General Ledger).
2. Set a filter range with data, click Export > Excel.
3. Open the file — the date column is left-aligned text like `08-08-2026`.
4. Sort ascending — rows sort alphabetically (`dd-mm`) rather than by actual date.

Root cause, `frappe/desk/query_report.py`:
```python
def format_fields(data: frappe._dict) -> None:
    ...
    elif col.get("fieldtype") == "Date":
        for row in data.result:
            ...
            row[index] = formatdate(val)   # <-- stringifies before Excel export
    elif col.get("fieldtype") == "Datetime":
        for row in data.result:
            ...
            row[index] = format_datetime(val)
```
This runs unconditionally in `_export_query()` before `build_xlsx_data()`/`make_xlsx()`, for both CSV and Excel branches — but only Excel has real cell types to lose.

**Expected behavior**

Excel export of a Date/Datetime column should produce a native Excel date/datetime cell (as `make_xlsx` already supports and does correctly when given a real `date`/`datetime` value), so it sorts and filters correctly in Excel — regardless of the display number format applied.

**Environment**
- Frappe version: `15.116.1` (`version-15`)
- Excel: reproduced with `openpyxl` writing/reading the exported `.xlsx`; also observed by a user in Excel for macOS
- System Settings Date Format: `dd-mm-yyyy` (reproduces with other non-ISO formats too)

**Suggested fix**

In `format_fields()`, only stringify Date/Datetime columns when building the CSV output, not the Excel output — since `build_xlsx_data`/`make_xlsx` already handle native date objects correctly and apply the System Settings date format as the cell's `number_format`.

issue.title: sanitize_html silently deletes <user@example.com> from a text/plain email body on version-16 (nh3 removes where bleach escaped)
issue.body:
## Description of the issue

On `version-16`, `sanitize_html` **deletes** a bare angle-bracket email address from a
**plain-text** email body. On `version-15` the same address was escaped and preserved.

The body is never HTML, but it is HTML-sanitized anyway, and the `bleach` → `nh3` swap
(#34740, backported in #36569) changed the outcome for a disallowed run from *escape* to *remove*.

`frappe/email/receive.py` already knows the content type — `set_content_and_type()` sets
`self.content_type` to `text/plain` or `text/html` — but the write does not consult it:

```python
# frappe/email/receive.py:748
communication.content = sanitize_html(self.replace_inline_images(communication._attachments))
```

Because this overwrites `Communication.content` at receive time, the original text is not
recoverable downstream: the raw message is still canonical, but the stored content every
application reads has already lost the address.

## Context information (for bug reports)

**Output of `bench version`**
```
Not run on a live v16 bench — I do not have one. Reproduced against branch source:
  version-16  @ 33bf510b17af  (v16.33.0, 2026-09-01)   nh3 0.3.7      -> address REMOVED
  version-15  @ 755b5cb81fab  (v15.120.0, 2026-09-01)  bleach 6.4.0   -> address ESCAPED
by importing each branch's own frappe/utils/html_utils.py. The snippet below should
reproduce directly on a real v16 bench.
```

## Steps to reproduce the issue

1. On a `version-16` bench, run:

```python
from frappe.utils.html_utils import sanitize_html

body = "Please copy my colleague <j.novak@example.com> on the confirmation."
print(repr(sanitize_html(body)))
```

2. Compare against the same call on `version-15`.
3. Or, end to end: send a **plain-text** email containing `<someone@example.com>` to a mailbox
   Frappe pulls, then read the resulting `Communication.content`.

### Observed result

```
'Please copy my colleague  on the confirmation.'
```

The address is gone, with no error and no indication anything was dropped.

### Expected result

```
'Please copy my colleague <j.novak@example.com> on the confirmation.'
```

i.e. the `version-15` behaviour — the text preserved, escaped if necessary.

### Stacktrace / full error message

```
None — this fails silently. Nothing raises; the message simply stores without the address.
```

## Additional information

**Why a plain-text body reaches the sanitizer at all.** The early-out in `sanitize_html` is:

```python
if not bool(BeautifulSoup(html, "html.parser").find()):
    return html
```

`html.parser` parses `<j.novak@example.com>` as an element, so `.find()` is truthy and the body is
treated as HTML:

```python
>>> BeautifulSoup("Please copy my colleague <j.novak@example.com> on the confirmation.", "html.parser").find()
<j.novak@example.com> on the confirmation.</j.novak@example.com>
```

`bleach` escaped that run, so the text survived. `nh3`/ammonia removes a disallowed element, so the
words are gone.

**Impact.** Anything reading an address out of a body: reply threading on quoted attribution lines
(`On <date>, Name <addr> wrote:`), contact extraction, forwarded third-party details. Non-English
quoted-reply lines are affected identically. Measured over a 25-message test corpus here, 7 lost an
address this way.

**Suggested fix.** Sanitize only when the content is actually HTML, at the `receive.py` call site:

```python
content = self.replace_inline_images(communication._attachments)
communication.content = sanitize_html(content) if self.content_type == "text/html" else content
```

Escaping rather than dropping inside `sanitize_html` would also work, but gating on the
already-known content type looks narrower and closer to the original intent.

Happy to open a PR in that shape if you'd like.

issue.title: Query Report Excel export writes Date/Datetime columns as text, breaking sort order
issue.body:
`frappe.desk.query_report.export_query` (used by every Script/Query Report's "Export" button, e.g. ERPNext's General Ledger) converts `Date`/`Datetime` columns to display-formatted strings via `format_fields()` *before* handing the data to the Excel writer. `frappe.utils.xlsxutils.make_xlsx` only writes a native, sortable Excel date cell when it receives an actual `datetime.date`/`datetime.datetime` — a string is written as plain text, so Excel sorts the column alphabetically instead of chronologically (e.g. with System Settings Date Format `dd-mm-yyyy`: `01-07-2026, 01-08-2026, 02-07-2026, 02-08-2026` instead of date order).

CSV export is unaffected in practice (CSV has no cell types, so Excel re-parses the text as a date when it opens the file), and List View / Report View export (`frappe.desk.reportview.export_query`) is also unaffected — it doesn't stringify dates. The bug is specific to the Query Report export path.

**To Reproduce**

1. Open any Query/Script Report with a Date column (e.g. Accounting > General Ledger).
2. Set a filter range with data, click Export > Excel.
3. Open the file — the date column is left-aligned text like `08-08-2026`.
4. Sort ascending — rows sort alphabetically (`dd-mm`) rather than by actual date.

Root cause, `frappe/desk/query_report.py`:
```python
def format_fields(data: frappe._dict) -> None:
    ...
    elif col.get("fieldtype") == "Date":
        for row in data.result:
            ...
            row[index] = formatdate(val)   # <-- stringifies before Excel export
    elif col.get("fieldtype") == "Datetime":
        for row in data.result:
            ...
            row[index] = format_datetime(val)
```
This runs unconditionally in `_export_query()` before `build_xlsx_data()`/`make_xlsx()`, for both CSV and Excel branches — but only Excel has real cell types to lose.

**Expected behavior**

Excel export of a Date/Datetime column should produce a native Excel date/datetime cell (as `make_xlsx` already supports and does correctly when given a real `date`/`datetime` value), so it sorts and filters correctly in Excel — regardless of the display number format applied.

**Environment**
- Frappe version: `15.116.1` (`version-15`)
- Excel: reproduced with `openpyxl` writing/reading the exported `.xlsx`; also observed by a user in Excel for macOS
- System Settings Date Format: `dd-mm-yyyy` (reproduces with other non-ISO formats too)

**Suggested fix**

In `format_fields()`, only stringify Date/Datetime columns when building the CSV output, not the Excel output — since `build_xlsx_data`/`make_xlsx` already handle native date objects correctly and apply the System Settings date format as the cell's `number_format`.

issue.title: Child-table Attach fields attach another user's private file (regression from #42163)
issue.body:
### Summary

Since #42163, `attach_files_to_document` walks child-table Attach / Attach Image fields and claims any orphan `File` whose `file_url` matches — with no check on who uploaded it. Saving a document is now enough to attach another user's private file to it, which grants that file's read permission to everyone who can read the document.

`version-16` is not affected: its `attach_files_to_document` still walks only the parent doctype's Attach fields.

### Where

`frappe/core/doctype/file/utils.py`, in `_attach_field_values`:

```python
orphan_by_url = {
    row.file_url: row.name
    for row in frappe.get_all(
        "File",
        filters={
            "attached_to_doctype": ["is", "not set"],
            "attached_to_name": ["is", "not set"],
            "attached_to_field": ["is", "not set"],
            "file_url": ["in", remaining_values],
        },
        fields=["name", "file_url"],
    )
}

for df, value in remaining:
    if orphan_name := orphan_by_url.get(value):
        frappe.db.set_value("File", orphan_name, field={...})
```

`frappe.get_all` here ignores permissions, and nothing in the path consults `File.owner`. `attach_files_to_document` is registered as `doc_events["*"]["on_update"]`, so it runs for every doctype, and it runs *after* the controller's own `on_update`.

### To reproduce

1. A doctype with a child table holding an `Attach Image` field.
2. User A uploads a private file. Note its `file_url`. It stays unattached, so only A can read it.
3. User B saves their own document, putting A's `file_url` into a child row's Attach field.
4. The `File` row is now `attached_to` B's document. Anyone who can read that document can read A's private file.

Guessing or reading a `/private/files/...` path off another page is enough; no access to the file is needed beforehand.

### Impact

Any app with a child-table Attach field is affected as soon as it tracks `develop`. It also silently overrides an app's own ownership rules: an app that deliberately declines to attach a file it does not trust has that decision reversed, because the framework hook runs last and re-attaches it.

We hit this in [frappe/gameplan](https://github.com/frappe/gameplan) on a profile "bento card" image field. Our `on_update` checks the uploader and declines; `attach_files_to_document` then attached the file anyway. Two tests that assert the ownership rule went red the day #42163 merged. We have worked around it by clearing the field value, but the framework behaviour still needs a fix.

### Suggested fix

Only adopt an orphan whose `owner` is the session user (or the document's owner), mirroring the rule apps have to apply themselves. Falling back to a `has_permission` check on the `File` would also work; the current unconditional `frappe.get_all` + `set_value` cannot distinguish a file the saver uploaded from one they merely named.

issue.title: sanitize_html silently deletes <user@example.com> from a text/plain email body on version-16 (nh3 removes where bleach escaped)
issue.body:
## Description of the issue

On `version-16`, `sanitize_html` **deletes** a bare angle-bracket email address from a
**plain-text** email body. On `version-15` the same address was escaped and preserved.

The body is never HTML, but it is HTML-sanitized anyway, and the `bleach` → `nh3` swap
(#34740, backported in #36569) changed the outcome for a disallowed run from *escape* to *remove*.

`frappe/email/receive.py` already knows the content type — `set_content_and_type()` sets
`self.content_type` to `text/plain` or `text/html` — but the write does not consult it:

```python
# frappe/email/receive.py:748
communication.content = sanitize_html(self.replace_inline_images(communication._attachments))
```

Because this overwrites `Communication.content` at receive time, the original text is not
recoverable downstream: the raw message is still canonical, but the stored content every
application reads has already lost the address.

## Context information (for bug reports)

**Output of `bench version`**
```
Not run on a live v16 bench — I do not have one. Reproduced against branch source:
  version-16  @ 33bf510b17af  (v16.33.0, 2026-09-01)   nh3 0.3.7      -> address REMOVED
  version-15  @ 755b5cb81fab  (v15.120.0, 2026-09-01)  bleach 6.4.0   -> address ESCAPED
by importing each branch's own frappe/utils/html_utils.py. The snippet below should
reproduce directly on a real v16 bench.
```

## Steps to reproduce the issue

1. On a `version-16` bench, run:

```python
from frappe.utils.html_utils import sanitize_html

body = "Please copy my colleague <j.novak@example.com> on the confirmation."
print(repr(sanitize_html(body)))
```

2. Compare against the same call on `version-15`.
3. Or, end to end: send a **plain-text** email containing `<someone@example.com>` to a mailbox
   Frappe pulls, then read the resulting `Communication.content`.

### Observed result

```
'Please copy my colleague  on the confirmation.'
```

The address is gone, with no error and no indication anything was dropped.

### Expected result

```
'Please copy my colleague <j.novak@example.com> on the confirmation.'
```

i.e. the `version-15` behaviour �� the text preserved, escaped if necessary.

### Stacktrace / full error message

```
None — this fails silently. Nothing raises; the message simply stores without the address.
```

## Additional information

**Why a plain-text body reaches the sanitizer at all.** The early-out in `sanitize_html` is:

```python
if not bool(BeautifulSoup(html, "html.parser").find()):
    return html
```

`html.parser` parses `<j.novak@example.com>` as an element, so `.find()` is truthy and the body is
treated as HTML:

```python
>>> BeautifulSoup("Please copy my colleague <j.novak@example.com> on the confirmation.", "html.parser").find()
<j.novak@example.com> on the confirmation.</j.novak@example.com>
```

`bleach` escaped that run, so the text survived. `nh3`/ammonia removes a disallowed element, so the
words are gone.

**Impact.** Anything reading an address out of a body: reply threading on quoted attribution lines
(`On <date>, Name <addr> wrote:`), contact extraction, forwarded third-party details. Non-English
quoted-reply lines are affected identically. Measured over a 25-message test corpus here, 7 lost an
address this way.

**Suggested fix.** Sanitize only when the content is actually HTML, at the `receive.py` call site:

```python
content = self.replace_inline_images(communication._attachments)
communication.content = sanitize_html(content) if self.content_type == "text/html" else content
```

Escaping rather than dropping inside `sanitize_html` would also work, but gating on the
already-known content type looks narrower and closer to the original intent.

Happy to open a PR in that shape if you'd like.

*(Not a security report — this is over-aggressive sanitization causing data loss, not unsafe
content getting through.)*

issue.title: Files uploaded into a child-table Attach field are never attached, so private ones become unreadable
issue.body:
## What happens

A file uploaded without `doctype` and `docname`, then written into an **Attach** or **Attach Image** field on a **child table**, is never attached to anything. The `File` row keeps `attached_to_doctype` and `attached_to_name` empty forever. No error is raised.

If that file is private, `File.has_permission` then denies read to everyone except the uploader and Administrator. Permanently. The same file in an Attach field on the *parent* doctype works fine.

## Why it happens

`attach_files_to_document` builds its field list from the parent's own meta only:

`frappe/core/doctype/file/utils.py` (develop, line 343):

```python
attach_fields = doc.meta.get("fields", {"fieldtype": ["in", ["Attach", "Attach Image"]]})
```

A parent doctype's meta contains a `Table` field, not the child doctype's fields, so an Attach field declared on a child doctype is never in that list.

The hook cannot see the child rows from the child side either. It is registered on `*` / `on_update` in `frappe/hooks.py` (develop, line 196), but **child documents never run `on_update`**:

- `Document.run_post_save_methods` (`frappe/model/document.py`) calls `self.run_method("on_update")` on the saved document only.
- `Document.update_child_table` writes rows with a bare `d.db_update()`. There is no `run_method` on a child row anywhere in that path.

So the parent's `on_update` is the only point where a child row's Attach field can be reached, and that is exactly what the current code does not do.

Once the file has no attachment, `has_permission` in `frappe/core/doctype/file/file.py` (develop, line 1015) runs out of ways to grant read. It allows a public file, the owner, a shared file, and then delegates to the attached document. With `attached_to_doctype` empty it falls through to the final `return False`.

Worth noting: `relink_mismatched_files`, in the same `utils.py`, already walks `doc.meta.get("fields", {"fieldtype": "Table"})` and reads each child doctype's Attach fields. So the traversal exists in the file. It just is not done by the function that assigns the attachment.

## Why this is not visible in Desk

Desk's attach control sends the parent's identity at upload time, so the file is already attached before `attach_files_to_document` ever runs. `frappe/public/js/frappe/form/controls/attach.js`, lines 82-84:

```js
options.doctype = this.frm.doctype;
options.docname = this.frm.docname;
options.fieldname = this.df.fieldname;
```

The gap shows up for the other pattern: upload the file first, get a `file_url` back, then set the field and save the document. That is the normal flow for an SPA frontend, and it is the case `attach_files_to_document` exists to handle.

## Reproduction

Run in `bench --site <site> console`. It creates a parent doctype with one Attach Image field and a child table whose rows also have an Attach Image field, uploads a private file for each, saves once, and compares.

```python
import base64
import os

import frappe
from frappe.core.doctype.file.file import has_permission

frappe.set_user("Administrator")
png = base64.b64decode(
    "iVBORw0KGgoAAAANSUhEUgAAAAEAAAABCAYAAAAfFcSJAAAADUlEQVR42mP8z8BQDwAEhQGAhKmMIQAAAABJRU5ErkJggg=="
)

frappe.get_doc({
    "doctype": "DocType", "name": "Repro Child", "module": "Core", "custom": 1, "istable": 1,
    "fields": [{"fieldname": "image", "fieldtype": "Attach Image", "label": "Image"}],
}).insert()

frappe.get_doc({
    "doctype": "DocType", "name": "Repro Parent", "module": "Core", "custom": 1, "autoname": "hash",
    "fields": [
        {"fieldname": "image", "fieldtype": "Attach Image", "label": "Parent Image"},
        {"fieldname": "rows", "fieldtype": "Table", "label": "Rows", "options": "Repro Child"},
    ],
    "permissions": [{"role": "All", "read": 1, "write": 1, "create": 1}],
}).insert()
frappe.db.commit()

# Distinct bytes per file, otherwise content-hash dedupe makes both point at one file_url.
f_parent = frappe.get_doc({"doctype": "File", "file_name": "repro-parent.png",
                           "is_private": 1, "content": png + os.urandom(16)}).insert()
f_child = frappe.get_doc({"doctype": "File", "file_name": "repro-child.png",
                          "is_private": 1, "content": png + os.urandom(16)}).insert()

frappe.get_doc({"doctype": "Repro Parent", "image": f_parent.file_url,
                "rows": [{"image": f_child.file_url}]}).insert()
frappe.db.commit()

f_parent.reload()
f_child.reload()
print("parent field:", f_parent.attached_to_doctype, f_parent.attached_to_name)
print("child  field:", f_child.attached_to_doctype, f_child.attached_to_name)

other = frappe.db.get_value("User", {"name": ("not in", ["Administrator", "Guest"]), "enabled": 1}, "name")
print("read by", other, "parent field file:", has_permission(f_parent, "read", other))
print("read by", other, "child  field file:", has_permission(f_child, "read", other))
```

### Observed

```
parent field: Repro Parent holkc94cgk
child  field: None None
read by outsider@example.com parent field file: True
read by outsider@example.com child  field file: False
```

The parent-field file gets attached and inherits the document's read permission. The child-field file gets nothing, and is denied even though the user can read the document the image belongs to.

### Expected

The child-field file should be attached too, so it inherits the same read permission as the parent-field file.

## Impact

Any app that puts an image on a child table and uploads it before the parent document exists ships a private file that only its uploader and Administrator can read. Nothing reports this: the upload succeeds, the field saves, the image renders correctly for the person who uploaded it, and every other user gets a broken image.

We hit this in Gameplan with a profile card image. `GP Profile Bento Card` is a child table with an Attach Image field. Card images were visible to their owner and 403 for everyone else. We worked around it with an `on_update` method on the parent doctype that walks its own child rows and attaches their images to the parent. That workaround should not be necessary, and every app with a child-table Attach field needs its own copy of it today.

## Verified and not verified

Verified by reading the source and by running the reproduction above:

- `attach_files_to_document` reads only `doc.meta` fields. The same line is present on `develop` (utils.py:343), `version-16` (utils.py:319) and `version-15` (utils.py:320).
- The hook is registered on `*` / `on_update` on all three branches.
- Child documents do not run `on_update`: `update_child_table` calls only `db_update()`, and `run_post_save_methods` runs `on_update` on the saved document.
- `has_permission` returns `False` for an unattached private file, and `True` for the same file once attached to a readable document.
- Over HTTP with no session, a private file returns 403 and a public one returns 200. Checked with `curl` against a local site.

Not verified:

- Only tested on `develop` (`frappe.__version__` reports `17.0.0-dev`), on MariaDB. The version-15 and version-16 claims are from reading those branches, not from running the reproduction there.
- Did not test the Desk grid attach flow end to end. The claim that Desk avoids this is from reading `attach.js`, not from clicking through it.
- Did not test submitted documents (`on_update_after_submit`), where the same hook is registered.

## Related

- #23296 and #38917 describe the neighbouring gap: a `File` has no way to point back at the specific child row it belongs to. Those are about a file that *is* attached to the parent but cannot identify its row. This report is about the case where the file is attached to nothing at all, which is a different failure and has a different consequence (permission denial rather than a stale link).
- #37435 and #33362 covered `attached_to_name` not being updated after a rename or after a temporary name, which `relink_mismatched_files` now handles for child tables. That function is the traversal this one is missing.

Updating everyone who had the old value only makes sense if you can also be sure all of them were pointing at the file that changed. But in this case we are not sure which one to update and leaving it as-it is

issue.title: Calendar and date picker ignore the user's language (date picker has no ja; FullCalendar locales dropped in v16)
issue.body:
## Description

Frappe's desk renders its calendar and date picker in English regardless of the user's language. There are four separate causes. Three are one-line omissions in code that already intends to be localised; one is a regression between v15 and v16.

Raising this as an issue rather than a PR: I opened #42343 and #42344 and both were closed automatically because I am not in `.github/VOUCHED.td`. The patches are linked below for whoever picks this up.

| | v15 | v16 / develop |
|---|---|---|
| Date picker shows English month and day names | affected | affected |
| Calendar shows English month names, day names and buttons | fine | **affected — regression** |
| Calendar forces a 12-hour clock | fine | affected |
| Relative dates ("3 days ago") stay English | affected | affected |

### 1. The date picker has no Japanese definition

`datepicker_i18n.js` defines 25 languages; Japanese is not among them, though Chinese and Thai are. `date.js` falls back to English for anything it cannot find:

```js
if (!$.fn.datepicker.language[lang]) {
    lang = "en";
}
```

So every date field in a Japanese desk shows English months and weekdays.

### 2. FullCalendar is given a locale it was never taught (v16 only — regression)

`calendar.js` passes `locale: frappe.boot.lang`, but `calendar.bundle.js` imports no locales, so FullCalendar has nothing to resolve the code against and silently renders English.

**v15 does not have this problem**: `calendar.js` pushes `assets/frappe/js/lib/fullcalendar/locale-all.js` into its assets, and that file includes `ja`. The locales were dropped in `def9630e1c` ("chore: move fullcalendar libs to a separate bundle") when the calendar moved to FullCalendar 6, and never re-added.

The translations are already in the dependency — `@fullcalendar/core/locales/ja.js` carries 前 / 次 / 今日 / 終日 / 予定リスト. Importing `locales-all` grows `calendar.bundle.js` from 258 KB to 293 KB, and that bundle is only fetched when a calendar view opens.

### 3. `eventTimeFormat` hard-codes `hour12: true` (v16 only)

Most locales do not use a 12-hour clock, and the site already records the answer in **System Settings → Time Format**. v15 derives it correctly from `get_user_time_fmt()`.

### 4. moment never leaves English

`setup_moment()` hard-codes `moment.locale("en")`. Changing that alone does nothing, because `moment-timezone-with-data-10-year-range.min.js` ships no locale data — `moment.locale("ja")` against it silently keeps English.

The locales have to be imported too, and that is not free: `moment/min/locales` adds **298 KB to `libs.bundle.js`** (739 → 1,038 KB, measured), on a bundle that loads on every desk page. That is a lot for "3 days ago", so it is worth deciding separately from 1–3; a dynamic import of the single locale in use would avoid the cost at the price of some complexity.

## To reproduce

1. Set a user's language to `ja` (or any language absent from `datepicker_i18n.js`).
2. Open any date field — month and weekday names are English.
3. On v16, open any Calendar view — month names, day names and buttons are English, and event times use a 12-hour clock whatever Time Format says.

## Patches

Ready and verified to apply cleanly, separated per branch since the causes differ:

- **v15** (`edae775dd3`) — date picker, moment
- **develop** (`b861fc68d7`) — date picker + FullCalendar locales + `hour12`, moment

https://github.com/lifegence/frappe-i18n-patches

Branches are also on https://github.com/masakazu-nomura2022/frappe, so #42343 and #42344 can be reopened with `/recheck` if someone is willing to vouch. Happy to rework any of it — particularly item 4, which I would understand you declining as it stands.

## Context

Found while localising a Frappe/ERPNext deployment into Japanese. A user in the business team asked simply for the calendar to be in Japanese; it turned out not to be a translation problem at all, since none of these libraries pass through Frappe's translation function.
